posts.text:
Redbelly Network has named Christian Westerlind Wigstrom as its new CEO. He starts in November 2026.

Who is he, and what could his track record mean for Tokeniser? A short, sourced thread.

https://redbelly.network/blog/redbelly-new-CEO-is-a-payments-pioneer-betting-on-regulated-tokenisation

image.alt: Redbelly DAO community briefing card. New CEO: Christian Westerlind Wigstrom. Role: Chief Executive Officer. Starts November 2026. Previously co-founder and CEO of Monoova.

posts.text:
2/8 Background

He co-founded Australian payments company Monoova and led it for about 9.5 years, growing what began as Moneytech Payments. He handed over the CEO role on 1 July 2026.

https://www.monoova.com/newsroom/monoova-appoints-bianca-bates-as-ceo

3/8 Monoova's record, as reported by the company:

– close to $200bn in payments processed since he joined
– transacts with more than 10% of all Australians
– FinTech Organisation of the Year at the 2022 Finnies

https://www.monoova.com/newsroom/monoova-appoints-bianca-bates-as-ceo
https://www.fintechaustralia.org.au/community-news/fintech-australia-announces-2022-finnies-award-winners

4/8 Monoova was a major player in PayTo, which lets a business take payments straight from a customer's bank account once the customer approves an agreement in their online banking.

In March 2024 it called itself Australia's largest PayTo facilitator.

https://www.aap.com.au/aapreleases/cision20240311ae57503/

5/8 Industry roles: elected to the FinTech Australia board in 2022, later its Treasurer. In 2025 he became an alternate director of AusPayNet, the payments industry's self-regulatory body.

https://www.fintechaustralia.org.au/community-news/fintech-australia-announces-new-board-appointments-2023
https://www.monoova.com/newsroom/christian-westerlind-wigstrom-appointed-as-alternate-director-at-australian-payments-network

6/8 What Redbelly said: he joins to lead its push into regulated tokenisation.

In his words: “In payments, I learnt that success belonged to the company that saw compliance as a product edge rather than a tick box.”

https://redbelly.network/blog/redbelly-new-CEO-is-a-payments-pioneer-betting-on-regulated-tokenisation

7/8 Why now: Australia's Digital Assets Framework Act commences in April 2027. And the RBA's Project Acacia report names Redbelly as one of three platforms used to test a pilot wholesale central bank digital currency.

https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2026A00038/asmade/text
https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/tokenised-money/pdf/project-acacia-final-report.pdf

8/8 Our read (analysis, not fact): Tokeniser may be run like payments infrastructure, sold via partners with compliance built in.

Open question: how payments experience carries over to capital markets.

Full briefing with sources: {BRIEFING_LINK}

Not financial advice.
